name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle designed to travel on no more than three wheels, ridden on a seat or saddle and steered with a handlebar; an electric two-wheeler whose motor exceeds five brake horsepower (3,750 W) is a full motorcycle rather than a motor-driven cycle. Defined by Revised Code of Washington §46.04.330; ESSB 6110 (Chapter 159, Laws of 2026) notes this definition covers many vehicles its narrower e-bike definition excludes, and has the Department of Licensing drafting an electric motorcycle framework due December 15, 2026 (interim) and October 31, 2027 (final).

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, handlebar steering, and no more than three wheels
Its motor produces more than five brake horsepower (3,750 W); one at or under that is a motor-driven cycle

Not an electric-assisted bicycle, moped or motorized foot scooter; since June 11, 2026, anything able to exceed 20 mph on its motor alone, or built to be switched out of e-bike limits, isn't an e-bike
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement
Every rider and passenger must wear a motorcycle helmet on a state highway, county road or city street
The operator must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windshield, and it needs mirrors on both sides
Registered and plated with the Department of Licensing, and must carry liability insurance
One ridden only off-road without street registration is an off-road vehicle instead
